_meta.source: California ELA/ELD Framework, Chapter 3: Content and Pedagogy — Transitional Kindergarten Through Grade One (California Department of Education, adopted by the State Board of Education July 2014)
_meta.scope_note: Writing-focused instructional moves extracted from Chapter 3 snapshots of practice, classroom vignettes, and the five key-theme guidance sections. Chapter 3 covers TK–Grade 1 only, so there are no 3–12 moves. TK and kindergarten moves are filed under "K"; grade one moves under "1-2"; span-wide moves presented for TK–1 are duplicated under both. Level keys map ELPAC / CA ELD proficiency to the student each move serves (1 = Emerging, 2 = low–mid Expanding, 3 = upper Expanding–lower Bridging, 4 = upper Bridging).

1.move: After clapping the syllables in each child's name during the read-aloud, hand every child a sticky note and have them write their own name on it, then place it in the column above the matching number of syllables on a class histogram chart.
1.language_target: syllable segmentation of one's own name (one to four syllables)
1.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.1: Tingo Tango Mango Tree (Integrated ELA and Mathematics in TK)

1.move: While the rest of the class works at literacy stations, sit with Emerging-level ELs and a teacher-made copy of the five-page Goldilocks book the children built, collaboratively retelling it page by page; prompt them to use the transition words 'then' and 'next' and point out past-tense verbs such as 'Baby Bear said' as you reread.
1.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.2: Goldilocks and the Three Bears (Integrated ELA and ELD in TK)

1.move: With the five story pictures and popsicle-stick puppets in front of your Emerging-level ELs, lead an echo retelling in which you state each event using past-tense verbs ('there were three little pigs,' 'the wolf blew the house down') and have the children repeat after you, telling them to listen for the verbs that show the story already happened.
1.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.2: Retelling The Three Little Pigs Using Past Tense Verbs and Expanded Sentences (Designated ELD in TK)

1.move: Close each storybook read-aloud lesson with a quick five-minute writing task (describe a character, answer a text-dependent question, or give an opinion), then jointly reconstruct the story aloud as you scribe, feeding in newly taught general academic words (e.g., scrumptious, encouraged) and story-grammar openers ('Once upon a time…,' 'After she went to sleep…').
1.language_target: temporal story openers 'Once upon a time…' / 'After …'; general academic vocabulary
1.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.7: Learning Two Languages in an Alternative Dual Language Program — Interacting with Storybooks: Principles for Planning

1.move: During designated ELD on the insect unit, give Emerging-level ELs an open sentence frame that targets grammar (e.g., 'When the bee lands on the flower, ___'), and coach them to add a familiar adjective to a noun (a big/small/green bee), drop in a simple prepositional phrase ('on the leaf'), and use precise domain words (larva, thorax) when they say and then write their observations.
1.language_target: noun-phrase expansion with adjectives; prepositional phrase 'on the leaf'; domain words larva/thorax
1.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.6: Expanding Science Observations, Designated ELD Connected to Science

1.move: Guide Emerging-level ELs to combine two short sentences from their science notes into a compound sentence with 'and' (e.g., 'Bees are insects.' + 'Bees make honey.' → 'Bees are insects, and they make honey.') before they write the combined sentence in their journals.
1.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.6: Expanding Science Observations, Designated ELD Connected to Science

1.move: When introducing a new general academic word during designated ELD, tell students its cognate in their primary language (e.g., 'furious' is 'furioso' in Spanish) and show them the place in the story where they first heard it before having them use it.
1.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.4: General Academic Vocabulary Instruction from Storybooks (Designated ELD in Kindergarten)

2.move: As the children draw conclusions about the name-syllable histogram, scribe their spoken observations onto the class chart beside the graph, deliberately writing in the comparison language they use ('more than,' 'fewer than,' 'the same number as').
2.language_target: comparison terms: more than / fewer than / the same number as
2.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.1: Tingo Tango Mango Tree (Integrated ELA and Mathematics in TK)

2.move: After charting the characters, setting, and plot events, have each child fold 12x18 construction paper into a five-page book and draw or cut the home in the forest, three bowls, three chairs, and three beds, then use Goldilocks-and-bears paper cutouts as props to retell the story to a partner page by page.
2.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.2: Goldilocks and the Three Bears (Integrated ELA and ELD in TK)

2.move: As each child dictates a sentence about the animal they painted for the alphabet mural, print the animal's name and the child's exact sentence on a large index card, pausing to prompt for more detail ('it swims in the ocean') and precise vocabulary ('it uses its enormous mouth to get lots of plankton').
2.language_target: descriptive detail and precise domain vocabulary (e.g., plankton)
2.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.3: Animal Informational Alphabet Books (Integrated ELA, Science, and Visual Arts in TK)

2.move: Write with and for the children every day—thinking aloud as you compose a text in front of them—so they see that print conveys meaning and can study the author's craft in the model you produce.
2.framework_anchor: Effective Expression: Writing (Key Themes, overview of the span)

2.move: Use the children's projected pictures of the five key story events to have partners take turns orally retelling the story, while you listen for their sequencing and language and note it before the class rewrites the story together.
2.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.1: Retelling and Rewriting The Three Little Pigs (Integrated ELA/Literacy and ELD in TK)

2.move: During the puppet retelling, model expanded sentences with a descriptive adjective and a prepositional phrase ('The frightened little pig ran into his house') and have the children say them chorally before they retell on their own.
2.language_target: noun-phrase expansion (adjective 'frightened') plus prepositional phrase 'into his house'
2.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.2: Retelling The Three Little Pigs Using Past Tense Verbs and Expanded Sentences (Designated ELD in TK)

2.move: Turn the jointly reconstructed English (and Spanish) story into an illustrated bilingual big book using photographs of the children acting it out, and place it in the library corner for repeated rereading.
2.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.1: Retelling and Rewriting The Three Little Pigs (Integrated ELA/Literacy and ELD in TK)

2.move: Have small groups draw an illustration of what they learned about litter and collaboratively decide on the words to label it, then present and explain the labeled illustration to the class.
2.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.4: Collecting and Reporting Data on Litter at School (Integrated ELA, ELD, Science, and History–Social Science)

2.move: Show Expanding-level ELs how to enrich a plain sentence with prepositional phrases (e.g., 'The bee is flying.' → 'The bee with full pollen baskets is flying around the flowers.'), point out where that kind of sentence appears in the read-aloud text, then have them expand their own science sentences before writing them.
2.language_target: prepositional-phrase expansion ('with full pollen baskets,' 'around the flowers')
2.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.6: Expanding Science Observations, Designated ELD Connected to Science

2.move: Guide Expanding-level ELs to combine two sentences into a complex sentence using a relative clause (e.g., 'Bees are insects.' + 'Bees make honey.' → 'Bees are insects that make honey.') and have them use the structure in their written science observations.
2.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.6: Expanding Science Observations, Designated ELD Connected to Science

2.move: Teach 4–5 general academic words a week with a fixed routine—contextualize the word in the story, give a child-friendly explanation in complete sentences with examples, guide use in one or two think-pair-shares with scaffolds, then check understanding—so students can reuse the words when they retell or compose their own stories.
2.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.4: General Academic Vocabulary Instruction from Storybooks (Designated ELD in Kindergarten)

2.move: Once a story has been read several times and its vocabulary taught, place copies in the library, writing, and listening centers and encourage children to retell, dramatize, and write their own (or an altered) version of it.
2.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.7: Learning Two Languages in an Alternative Dual Language Program — Extending Understandings

3.move: Before the paired discussions and the class letter, review and write the key general academic words (discard, accumulate, observe, impact) and domain-specific words (habitat, pollute, litter) on a chart, and keep it visible so children pull the terms into their talk and writing.
3.language_target: general academic + domain-specific vocabulary (discard, accumulate, habitat, pollute, litter)
3.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.4: Collecting and Reporting Data on Litter at School (Integrated ELA, ELD, Science, and History–Social Science)

3.move: Acting as scribe, lead the class in jointly composing a letter to the principal that reports their litter findings, working the unit's special terminology into the text, then guide the group to revise and edit it together before presenting it.
3.language_target: domain terminology used in persuasive writing
3.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.4: Collecting and Reporting Data on Litter at School (Integrated ELA, ELD, Science, and History–Social Science)

3.move: Provide an optional sentence frame ('We should add/change ___ as a rule because ___.') so children who need support can state—and then write—their opinions about which classroom rules to change or add.
3.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.5: David Goes to School (Integrated ELA and Civics in Kindergarten)

3.move: Use a 'Story Rewriting Template' labeled with the metalanguage orientation, complication, and resolution to guide students as they jointly reconstruct the read-aloud story aloud while you scribe each stage of the narrative.
3.language_target: metalanguage for story stages: orientation / complication / resolution
3.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.1: Retelling and Rewriting The Three Little Pigs (Integrated ELA/Literacy and ELD in TK)

3.move: As you scribe the joint story reconstruction, prompt children to replace plain verbs with vivid ones—recasting 'the wolf knocked it down' as 'destroyed' or 'demolished' and eliciting words like 'ferocious'—and add their richer wording to the class text.
3.language_target: vivid past-tense verbs and adjectives (destroyed, demolished, ferocious)
3.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.1: Retelling and Rewriting The Three Little Pigs (Integrated ELA/Literacy and ELD in TK)

3.move: At the complication stage of the reconstruction, elicit a signal word ('Suddenly') and write 'Suddenly, a ferocious wolf came along…' so children learn to use language that marks the shift into the problem of a narrative.
3.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.1: Retelling and Rewriting The Three Little Pigs (Integrated ELA/Literacy and ELD in TK)

3.move: On day five of the read-aloud sequence, jointly reconstruct the story as you write it under a document camera for all to see, scaffolding sophisticated language and helping children extend and refine each sentence.
3.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.3: Interactive Storybook Read Aloud (Integrated ELA/Literacy and ELD in Kindergarten)

3.move: At the end of the week, have pairs compose and illustrate either a retelling of the read-aloud story or an alternate version of it with different characters or a new ending.
3.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.3: Interactive Storybook Read Aloud (Integrated ELA/Literacy and ELD in Kindergarten)

3.move: Have children share their finished writing with peers and respond to classmates' questions and suggestions, then add details to strengthen the piece so it better communicates their ideas.
3.framework_anchor: Effective Expression: Writing (Key Themes, overview of the span) — W.K–1.5

1.move: Pair a newcomer Emerging-level EL with a bilingual buddy, model simple words and phrases ('yes,' 'no,' 'what's that?,' 'I think…'), and have her label her drawings with content words (pollen, bee, fly) so she can contribute to the bee unit in writing from the start.
1.language_target: labeling drawings with content words (pollen, bee, fly)
1.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.5: Interactive Read Alouds with Informational Texts (Integrated ELA, Literacy, and Science in Grade One)

1.move: During designated ELD, give Emerging-level ELs sequencing sentence frames ('First, you ___. Then, you ___. Next, you ___.') to explain—and then write down—the steps they took to solve a math word problem.
1.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.10: Mathematical Word Problems (Designated ELD Connected to Mathematics in Grade One)

2.move: Give Expanding-level ELs sentence frames that push extended, causal explanations ('First, you ___, because ___. After that, you have to ___ so you can see ___.') as they explain and then record how they solved a math word problem.
2.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.10: Mathematical Word Problems (Designated ELD Connected to Mathematics in Grade One)

2.move: Model 'unpacking' a dense science sentence by writing the original on a sentence strip in a pocket chart ('As the forager bee collects nectar, she carries pollen from flower to flower') and pulling shorter strips beneath it that each state one simple idea, thinking aloud as you go.
2.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.6: Unpacking Sentences (Designated ELD in Grade One)

2.move: After unpacking a sentence, post a strip showing the connector's meaning ('as' = at the same time; 'while' = at the same time), then have students join two of their own simple sentences with 'as' or 'while' and discover that the clause order can flip.
2.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.6: Unpacking Sentences (Designated ELD in Grade One)

2.move: Write with and for the children every day—thinking aloud as you compose a text in front of them—so they see that print conveys meaning and can study the author's craft in the model you produce.
2.framework_anchor: Effective Expression: Writing (Key Themes, overview of the span)

3.move: After a close reread, give students the frame 'This part is mostly about ___,' have them preface their idea to a partner using textual evidence, and record the agreed main idea on a chart they will later draw on when writing their own informational text.
3.language_target: main-idea frame 'This part is mostly about ___.'
3.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.5: Interactive Read Alouds with Informational Texts (Integrated ELA, Literacy, and Science in Grade One)

3.move: Have children examine and discuss the purpose of an informational text's Table of Contents, then, when they write their own informational books, guide them to organize the information and add headings and a Table of Contents modeled on the books they explored.
3.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.8: Examining a Table of Contents in Grade One

3.move: On chart paper, build a Frayer Model for a key domain word (e.g., metamorphosis)—definition, characteristics, examples, and non-examples—recording students' contributions, then have teams make their own Frayer Model for a chosen unit term using books for reference and present it to the group.
3.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.9: Teaching Science Vocabulary (Integrated ELA, ELD, and Science in Grade One)

3.move: Point students to a posted 'language frames for conversations' chart ('I agree, and ___. I agree, but ___.') and a target-word frame ('One thing that's important about metamorphosis is ___.') so they use precise academic talk that they then put into their charts and writing.
3.language_target: agreement frames; 'One thing that's important about ___ is ___.'
3.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.9: Teaching Science Vocabulary (Integrated ELA, ELD, and Science in Grade One)

3.move: Build a semantically grouped 'bee word wall' with illustrations and photos (e.g., anatomy terms head, thorax, abdomen, proboscis grouped together), add new terms as the unit unfolds, and have children reference it as they write their own informational texts about bees.
3.language_target: semantically grouped domain vocabulary (head, thorax, abdomen, proboscis)
3.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.5: Interactive Read Alouds with Informational Texts (Integrated ELA, Literacy, and Science in Grade One)

3.move: For the culminating project, have each child plan and write an illustrated informational book with a contents page (e.g., Introduction, Bee anatomy, Pollination, Honey), drawing on the word wall, posted charts, sentence frames, and mentor texts, then read it aloud from the 'Author's Chair.'
3.framework_anchor: Vignette 3.5: Interactive Read Alouds with Informational Texts (Integrated ELA, Literacy, and Science in Grade One)

3.move: Teach the unit's key general academic and domain words (courage, determination, honesty) for deep conceptual understanding rather than short definitions, and give children frames that embed the words ('I show responsibility when I ___. Honesty is important because ___.') for use in collaborative talk and writing.
3.language_target: abstract concept vocabulary (courage, determination, honesty, responsibility)
3.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.11: Expanding Sentences and Building Vocabulary (Designated ELD Connected to ELA/Social Studies in Grade One)

3.move: Have children share their finished writing with peers and respond to classmates' questions and suggestions, then add details to strengthen the piece so it better communicates their ideas.
3.framework_anchor: Effective Expression: Writing (Key Themes, overview of the span) — W.K–1.5

4.move: With Bridging-level ELs, build opinion sentence frames seeded with target vocabulary ('My favorite hero is ___ because ___. ___ was very courageous when ___.') and teach them to expand ideas by adding where/when/how (e.g., 'She worked on a farm' → 'She worked on a farm in the central valley of California'), then have them write short, text-evidence-based summaries of their discussions.
4.language_target: sentence expansion with prepositional/adverbial detail (where, when, how)
4.framework_anchor: Snapshot 3.11: Expanding Sentences and Building Vocabulary (Designated ELD Connected to ELA/Social Studies in Grade One)
